visualReview.notes: Inspected the complete palace from four directions and the current close frames of the eight Ionic half-columns, entrance statues and shield, open court, rear oval bay and side terrace. The top-down placement view retains the open court and both covered connections.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected ten geographic flat-fixture frames including the plaza front and courtyard. Stone, glazing, metal and roof surfaces remain legible at the relevant distances. The flat fixture covers the low courtyard surface. Its paving and fountain appear in the original-field and contextual captures. Shared material and unload checks passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected the 26 current frames, including four detail levels and transition views. The two blocks, angled footprint, deep court and rear oval bay survive the reductions. The upper balustrade, columns, windows, statues and paving resolve in the closest views. Triangle counts are 618, 3968, 15146 and 25354.

geographicReview.notes: The verified geographic boundary anchors the palace to the named Porto Alegre relation. The independent, original 256 m terrain field shows the plaza slope and greater exposure of the lower walls at the rear. The entrance stair and the terrace-to-grade contacts are estimated.

fidelityReview.scope: Standing Piratini Palace in Porto Alegre, with the government and residential wings, open courtyard and connecting passages, main Ionic frontage, roof terraces and rounded south end.
fidelityReview.notes: The IPHAN restoration report and state building inspection establish the government and residential wings, Ionic facade and doorway trim, Landowski statues, shield, roof terraces and open court. Floor heights, window bay spacing and roof equipment are estimates. The statues and courtyard fountain use simplified forms.

imageryReview.notes: Started with the locally published Qualla inventory and exact native Commons records. The interior photograph with assumed authorship and the modern attribution-only exterior photographs were excluded. The reconstruction uses written government and restoration records, original elevation and the mapped multipolygon.

primaryFactsReview.notes: Native palace and court boundaries are preserved. The restoration and building survey establish the Ionic order, two visible facade levels, statuary positions, and separate terraces and storey counts. Heights and ornamental profiles are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing government wing, residential wing and open court of Piratini Palace in Porto Alegre.

limitations: The model represents the standing exterior of the government and residential wings and their open internal courtyard. Roof furniture, floor elevations, step dimensions, grille patterns, and minor rear openings are estimated.
The original terrain sets the elevation change from the plaza to the rear. Entrance height, the local sidewalk landing, and lower wing contacts are approximate.

The documented eight engaged Ionic shafts, open balustrades, coat of arms, and Landowski sculpture locations are represented by authored geometry and simplified carving. Existing public Qualla candidates were screened first. The published interior view has assumed authorship, and the remaining exterior candidates used attribution terms or lacked confirmation of the exact original publication.
